EXPEDITED REVIEW: This plat is being pursued as an County expedited application, as it is within
the 1-mile boundary. An expedited review process is a concurrent preliminary and final plat.A project
may be eligiblefor an expedited review when theproposal containsno significant planning, design and
engineering issues. In other words proposals that meet all applicable regulations and generally meet the
review criteriafor preliminary andfinal plat may be eligiblefor the concurrent preliminary andfinal plat
process.
Staff recommends allowing the plat to proceed as anexpedited application.
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
This application is to allowforthe division of a single lot into 4 in order to accommodate individual
ownership of 3four-plexes that are nearly finished in their construction.The fourth lot will continue to be
held in a single ownership, and has 17 four-plexes either proposed or constructed on it, as well as the
detention facilities. This County subdivision was platted originally in 2010 and drainage and traffic
issues were addressed at that time. The subdivision is rapidly approaching buildout.As indicated, this
plat is being processed as an expedited review in the City, and has already been approved through the
County process.
PLAT DATA: In reviewing, providing comments, and making recommendations and decisions ona
proposed preliminary plat, the Staff, Planning Commission and City Council shalluse the following
criteria:
PLAN CHEYENNE.The application is in accordance with the development policies and physical patterns
identified in the Plan Cheyenne.
Plan Cheyenne calls out Urban Residential as the Future Land Use for this area.The Urban Residential
category allows forabroader variety of residential types, including single-family residences, duplexes,

patio homes, townhomes, condominiums and apartment. Supporting and complementary uses, including
open space and recreation, schools, places of worship and other public or civic uses are encouraged.It is
not the intent of this plan to change existing stable neighborhoods with single family residential
development, except those where redevelopment is desirable.
This application is in conformance with a number of Policies outlined in Plan Cheyenne
PLANNING.The application reflects sound planning and urban design principles with respect to existing
and potential future development in the vicinity, including consideration of current and future streets,
openspaces, blocks andlots, and public utilities or facilities.
This application creates separate ownership for three 4-plex structure, and leaves the remaining parcel
relatively unchanged.As previously stated, a majority of the infrastructure has already been constructed,
and does not change with this County Plat. A platted easement across the parking lot allows for
continued access to each structure.
STANDARDs.Division ofland meets the purposes, intent, and all applicable standards in Article4.
This land is being developed in the County, and there are no community facility fees due to the City. In
the event that annexation of this area is applied for and approved, community facility fes may be
required at the time of annexation.
The City will not have any maintenance or other responsibility for the road networks established here.A
road network plan was not submitted. The assumption is that they will be tying into the adjacent street
network, which appear to be adequate with Fox Farm Rd immediately adjacent to these lots to the north
and Montalto Road built to County standards.The City does not have any maintenance responsibilities
for any of the roads associated with this subdivision.
PHASING.Any phasing proposed in the application is clearly indicated and demonstrates a logical and
the subdivision within each phase compared to the anticipated timing or the likelihood of future phases
being constructed asplanned.
No phasing is proposed.
STUDi Es.The impacts identified in specific studies or technical reports that were prepared orrequested
to be prepared in association with the application, and whether the findings and recommendations of
these reports or any modifications or conditions on approval of the application, can mitigate these
impacts.
As only the lot lines are changing, and most of the construction has already occurred,
no additional studies were required for this replat.All applicable studies were submitted with the first
filing in 2010.

ZONING.Allproposed lots shall be build able lots according to the existing or proposed zoning district
standards, and result in site design and development patterns that meet the Intent and Applicability
statements of the existing or proposed zoning district.All parcels not proposed as build able lots and
whicharenot dedicated to and accepted by the City shall have a clearly defined entity responsible for
ongoing maintenance.
Lots already have structures on them and were reviewed for compliance with the County zoning
regulations by the Laramie County Planning Department at the time of development.
SURROUNDING DEVELOPMENT.The application will notcreate any undue influence onexisting or
potential development for adjacent property considering the existing zoning and Comprehensive Plan
policies for that property.
This plat will not have an effect on what is currently platted on this site nor willit impact the surrounding
greater than it already is.
